ሰላም ሰላም! ውድ የEthioFresh ቤተሰቦች፤ እንኳን ወደ Economics Chapter 3 Part 1 በሰላም መጣችሁ! ዛሬ ደግሞ የትምህርታችንን አዲስ ምዕራፍ ይዘንላችሁ ቀርበናል። በምዕራፍ 2 ስለ Demand, Supply እና Market Equilibrium በስፋት ማየታችን ይታወሳል። ዛሬ ደግሞ ከክፍል 3.1 (Consumer Preferences) ጀምሮ እስከ 3.3.1 (Cardinal Utility Theory) ድረስ ያሉትን ቁልፍ ሀሳቦች፣ ሰንጠረዦች፣ ግራፎች እና አዝናኝ የፈተና መስሪያ ስሌቶች (Numerical Examples) በከፍተኛ ጥራት አዘጋጅተንላችኋል። ሳታስቡት Economicsን ቀላል አድርገን እንጨርሰዋለን፤ አብራችሁን ቆዩ!👇👇👇


3. Theory of Consumer Behaviour

In our day-to-day life, we buy different goods and services for consumption. As consumers, we act to derive satisfaction by using goods and services. But have you ever thought of how you or any other person decides to buy those consumption goods and services? Consumer theory is based on what people like, so it begins with something that we cannot directly measure, but must infer. That is, consumer theory is based on the premise that we can infer what people like from the choices they make.

Consumer behaviour can be best understood in three steps:
1. Consumer Preferences: We need a practical way to describe how people prefer one good to another.
2. Budget Constraints: Consumers have limited incomes that restrict the quantities of goods they can buy.
3. Consumer Choice: Putting consumer preference and budget constraint together to determine consumer choice.

👉 • በየቀኑ የምንገዛቸውን እቃዎች እንዴት እንመርጣለን? የConsumer Theory ዋና ሃሳብ የሰዎችን ፍላጎት በቀጥታ መለካት ስለማንችል ከሚያደርጉት ምርጫ እንረዳዋለን የሚል ነው።
• እዚህ ላይ ሶስት ዋና ዋና ነገሮችን እናያለን፡ የሰውየው ፍላጎት (Preferences)፣ ያለው ገንዘብ ገደብ (Budget Constraints) እና የመጨረሻው ምርጫ (Consumer Choice)።


3.1 Consumer Preferences

A consumer makes choices by comparing bundles of goods. Given any two consumption bundles, the consumer either decides that one of the consumption bundles is strictly better than the other, or decides that she is indifferent between the two bundles.

In order to tell whether one bundle is preferred to another, we see how the consumer behaves in choice situations involving two bundles:
• Strict Preference: If a consumer always chooses bundle X when Y is available, we say the consumer strictly prefers X to Y, written as X > Y.
• Indifference: If the consumer is equally satisfied consuming bundle X or bundle Y, we say the consumer is indifferent between X and Y, written as X ~ Y.
• Weak Preference: If the consumer prefers or is indifferent between two bundles, we say she weakly prefers X to Y, written as X ≥ Y.

Preference Relations Summary:
• If X ≥ Y and Y ≥ X, then X ~ Y (The consumer treats both bundles equally).
• If X ≥ Y but it is NOT the case that X ~ Y, then X > Y (X is strictly better than Y).

👉 • ሁለት የእቃዎች ስብስብ (Bundles) ቢሰጥህ፣ አንዱን ከሌላው አብልጠህ ትመርጣለህ (Strict Preference: X > Y)፣ ወይም ሁለቱም እኩል ደስ ይሉሃል (Indifference: X ~ Y)፣ ወይም ደግሞ ቢያንስ ከሌላው ያላነሰ ይበልጥብሃል (Weak Preference: X ≥ Y)። ልክ በምግብ ቤት ሁለት ሜኑ ቀርቦልህ እንደመምረጥ ማለት ነው!


3.2 The Concept of Utility

Economists use the term utility to describe the satisfaction or pleasure derived from the consumption of a good or service. In other words, utility is the power of the product to satisfy human wants. Given any two consumption bundles X and Y, the consumer definitely wants the X-bundle rather than the Y-bundle if and only if the utility of X is better than the utility of Y.

Key points to bear in mind when defining utility:
• 'Utility' and 'Usefulness' are not synonymous: Paintings by Picasso may be useless functionally, but offer great utility to art lovers. Hence, usefulness is product-centric whereas utility is consumer-centric.
• Utility is subjective: The utility of a product varies from person to person. Non-smokers do not derive any utility from cigarettes.
• Utility varies by time and place: The utility we get from drinking coffee early in the morning may be different from the utility we get during lunch time.

💡 Exam Hint: በፈተና ላይ "Utility = Usefulness" የሚል True/False ጥያቄ ቢመጣ FALSE በሉ! Usefulness የእቃው ጥቅም ሲሆን፣ Utility ግን የሰውየው የእርካታ መጠን (Satisfaction) ነው። በተጨማሪም Utility Subjective ነው (ከሰው ሰው ይለያያል)።

👉 • Utility ማለት አንድን እቃ በመጠቀማችን የምናገኘው የእርካታ መጠን (Satisfaction) ነው። Utility እና Usefulness (ጠቃሚነት) አንድ አይደሉም! ለምሳሌ ሲጋራ ለጤና ጠቃሚ አይደለም (Not Useful) ነገር ግን አጫሹ እርካታ ያገኝበታል (Has Utility)።


3.3 Approaches of Measuring Utility

There are two major approaches to measure or compare consumer's utility:
1. Cardinal Utility Approach: Utility can be measured objectively using numerical values.
2. Ordinal Utility Approach: Utility is not measurable in cardinal numbers; rather, the consumer can rank or order choices.

3.3.1 The Cardinal Utility Theory
According to cardinal utility theory, utility is measurable by arbitrary units of measurement called utils in the form of 1, 2, 3, etc. For example, we may say that consumption of an orange gives Bilen 10 utils and a banana gives her 8 utils. From this, we can assert that Bilen gets more satisfaction from an orange than from a banana.

Assumptions of Cardinal Utility Theory:
1. Rationality of consumers: The main objective of the consumer is to maximize satisfaction given a limited budget.
2. Utility is cardinally measurable: Satisfaction of each commodity is measurable in subjective units called utils.
3. Constant marginal utility of money: A given unit of money deserves the same value at any time or place it is spent.
4. Diminishing Marginal Utility (DMU): The utility derived from each successive unit of a commodity diminishes as quantity consumed increases.
5. Total utility depends on quantities: If there are n commodities, TU = f(X1, X2, ..., Xn).

👉 • Cardinal Approach እርካታን ቁጥር ሰጥተን መለካት እንችላለን ይላል (ለምሳሌ ብርቱካን 10 utils፣ ሙዝ 8 utils ይሰጠኛል ብሎ መናገር)። ዋና Assumption-ኦቹ፡ ተማሪው Rational ነው፣ የብር Marginal Utility አይቀየርም፣ እና በበላህ ቁጥር እርካታህ እየቀነሰ ይሄዳል (DMU) የሚሉት ናቸው።

Total and Marginal Utility:
• Total Utility (TU): The total satisfaction a consumer gets from consuming a specific quantity of a commodity at a particular time.
• Marginal Utility (MU): The extra satisfaction a consumer realizes from an additional unit of the product. Graphically, it is the slope of total utility.

Formula:
MU = ΔTU / ΔQ

Key Relationships (MUST KNOW):
• When TU is increasing, MU is positive (MU > 0).
• When TU is maximized (Saturation Point), MU is zero (MU = 0).
• When TU is decreasing, MU is negative (MU < 0).

💡 Exam Hint: ፈተና ላይ TU Maximize በሚሆንበት ጊዜ MU ስንት ነው? ተብሎ መጠየቁ አይቀርም! መልሱ MU = 0 ነው። ይህ ነጥብ Saturation Point ይባላል።

👉 • TU ማለት አጠቃላይ ያገኘነው እርካታ ነው። MU ደግሞ ተጨማሪ 1 እቃ ስንጨምር የምናገኘው ተጨማሪ እርካታ ነው። ለምሳሌ 1ኛውን ውሃ ስትጠጣ በጣም ደስ ይልሃል (High MU)፣ 6ኛው ላይ ትረካለህ (TU Max, MU=0)፣ 7ኛውን በግድ ብትጠጣ ግን ያስመልስሃል (MU Negative ይሆናል)! 😂

Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility (LDMU):
The law of diminishing marginal utility states that as the quantity consumed of a commodity increases per unit of time, the utility derived from each successive unit decreases, consumption of all other commodities remaining constant.

Assumptions of LDMU:
• The consumer is rational.
• The consumer consumes identical/homogeneous products (same quality, color, design).
• There is no time gap in consumption.
• Consumer taste/preferences remain unchanged.

👉 • LDMU ማለት አንድን ነገር በተደጋጋሚ በተከታታይ በበላህ/በጠቀምክ ቁጥር ከእያንዳንዱ ተጨማሪ እቃ የምታገኘው እርካታ እየቀነሰ ይሄዳል የሚል ህግ ነው። ግን እቃዎቹ አንድ አይነት መሆን አለባቸው (ያለ እረፍት በደቂቃዎች ልዩነት እንደመጠጣት)።

Equilibrium of a Consumer:
The objective of a rational consumer is to maximize total utility. Given a limited income and market prices, what combination of goods and services should he/she consume?

a) The Case of One Commodity:
The equilibrium condition of a consumer consuming a single good X occurs when the marginal utility of X is equal to its market price:
MUX = PX


• If MUX > PX: The satisfaction is higher than the price, so the consumer should consume more X.
• If MUX < PX: The cost is higher than satisfaction, so the consumer should consume less X.
• If MUX = PX: The consumer is at equilibrium.

b) The Case of Two or More Commodities:
For two or more goods, consumer equilibrium is achieved when the marginal utility per money spent is equal for each good purchased and total income is fully spent:
(MUX / PX) = (MUY / PY) = ... = (MUN / PN)
and PXQX + PYQY + ... + PNQN = M


Numerical Example: Consumer Equilibrium Calculation
Suppose Saron has 7 Birr income (M = 7) to spend on two goods: Banana (P1 = 1 Birr) and Bread (P2 = 4 Birr).

Solution:
1. Equate Marginal Utility per Birr (MU1 / P1 = MU2 / P2):
Looking at the table, MU / P = 3 happens when Saron consumes 3 Bananas (3/1 = 3) and 1 Bread (12/4 = 3).
2. Check Income Constraint (P1Q1 + P2Q2 = M):
(1 × 3) + (4 × 1) = 3 + 4 = 7 Birr. The income condition is satisfied!
3. Total Utility at Equilibrium:
TU = TUbanana + TUbread = (6 + 5 + 3) + 12 = 14 + 12 = 26 utils.

Limitations of the Cardinal Approach:
1. The assumption that utility can be measured absolutely/objectively is unrealistic.
2. The assumption of constant marginal utility of money is unrealistic because as income increases, the marginal utility of money decreases.

👉 • ተጠቃሚው በጀት ስላለው Equilibrium (ሚዛናዊ እርካታ) ላይ የሚደርሰው (MUX / PX) = (MUY / PY) ሲሆንና ያለውን ብር ሙሉ በሙሉ ሲጠቀም ነው። የሳሮን ምሳሌ ላይ 3 ሙዝና 1 ዳቦ ስትገዛ ያላት 7 ብር ያልቃል፣ የሁለቱም እርካታ በወጣው ብር ልክ እኩል 3 ይሆናል! Cardinal approach ግን "የሰው እርካታ በቁጥር አይለካም" በሚል ይነቀፋል።
